newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly lower again.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly lower again.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended sharply lower again Wednesday, with gold and platinum futures seeing fresh life-of-contract lows across the board.

"It's a continuation of the erosion in the precious metals complex that's been going on for some time, driven by funds, rather than central bank activity," Merrill Lynch commodity research director, William O'Neill said.
"Today though there was the extra spur from the GFMS report, some more fund selling and some Australian producer hedging," he said.
COMEX February gold ended down $2.90 an ounce at $356.80, after posting a new contract low at $355.30, on estimated total volume for the gold strip at 55,000 lots.

In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $355.70/356.10 an ounce, after gold fixed at $356.60 in London Wednesday afternoon, just up from the morning fix at $355.80, which was the lowest fix since October 6, 1993.
COMEX March silver closed down 5.0 cents at $4.660 an ounce, but the low from Monday at $4.635 had not been broken yet, traders noted.

But spot gold prices have fallen about 3.5 percent in the first four trading days of 1997, and the further slump Wednesday was partly inspired by a report from industry consultants, Gold Fields Mineral Services (GFMS), which said a rise in official sector sales was the main cause of gold prices weakness in late 1996, traders said.
Official sector sales amounted to an estimated 123 tonnes in the second half of 1996, to give an estimated 208 tonnes total for the year, GFMS said.
Meanwhile, investment demand for physical bullion and gold coins remained at its lowest level since the 1970s, with the US stock market setting new record highs.

However, in data for Tuesday, released Wednesday morning, open interest in nearby active February gold futures fell 2,346 lots, while April gold open interest was down 2,261 lots, suggesting some fund shortcovering was occuring, traders said.
Total open interest in gold rose 11,572 lots in the previous four days to 201,377 lots Monday.

In addition, standard momentum indicators reached oversold levels Monday with the standard five-day slow stochastic falling to only four percent and the nine-day RSI (relative strength indicator) down to nine percent, suggesting a further period of consolidation may be due, analysts said.
"The target remains $350 on the downside though," Rosko Futures president John Rosko of New York said.
After reaching oversold levels on the daily charts Monday, nearby active March silver futures were also beginning to find some support from the trade, Rosko said.

Based on the closing price for the third quarter 1996 and implied volatility levels in options for the first quarter of 1997, the quarterly implied price range to two standard deviations for April gold was $399.85-342.95, McCarthy Crisanti Maffei (MCM) analyst, Peter McTeague, said.
April gold is the next most active gold contract, after February, withe open interest of 27,434 lots and it closed at $358.60 Wednesday, down $3.00 an ounce.
NYMEX April platinum closed down $3.20 an ounce at $363.80, after seeing a new contract low at $362.20, while earlier platinum fixed at a new three year low at $358.50 in London Wednesday morning.
NYMEX March palladium ended up $1.15 at $123.60 though.
"Palladium remains the odd man out in the complex, having lost very little ground since Christmas," O'Neill said.
"Industrial demand remains good and there's been only light selling from the Russians," he added.
